about: Babylon about 570 BC as grey blocks at true scale. Positions are UTM zone 38N metres (E, N); levels are metres in the German excavation zero (+0.0 = 25.5 m above sea level). Every block names the class of its plan and of its height: M measured (read off a dug outline on the sheets, or a dug size in print), R reasoned (drawn on the sheets but not dug, or set from a text or a scholar's inference), G guessed (ours).

says: The West Outwork's top at +12 is ours; Pedersén reconstructs it '(quite provisionally)' at +18 (P2021 p. 69).

Etemenanki: the stages follow the Esagila tablet, a later school text's figures, read at about 6 m to the gar. Its first stage stands on the measured base, 91.5 m; the tower above its base is shown as guessed, about 90 m in all.
alternatives: Etemenanki in Pedersén's model (P2021 Fig. 4.18, C6.2): stage sides 91.5, 80.5, 69.8, 60.2, 48.8, 38.0 and about 27 m; 91.5 m high in one model; the first terrace about 30 m, its top about +26 (P2021 p. 158, 164).
Etemenanki on the tablet: the base 15 gar, about 90 m (P2021 p. 159), against the 91.5 m measured; a first terrace of 15 m (the father's 30 cubits, P2021 p. 158) is a third reading.
Etemenanki's height: the proposals run from about 66 to about 90 m (a 2005 study; the tablet's sum).
